evals.name: invoices-prototype-review
evals.prompt: Can you critique the invoices prototype in docs/design/invoices? I'm sending it to the client Friday and want to know what's weak before they see it. Don't change the screens.
evals.expected_output: A critique of the three invoice pages (list.html, list-empty.html, detail.html), judged against DESIGN.md, docs/design/tokens.css and docs/design/flows/invoices/flows.md, with each finding located, the worst first, a plain statement that the prototype is not ready to send as it stands, and nothing in the prototype changed or committed, and no tool debris left unmentioned. From the tokens it computes that light muted text (#8b93a1) is about 3.1:1 on white, that white on the amber button is about 3.2:1, and that detail.html's hardcoded #fff summary panel leaves near-white dark-theme text at about 1.2:1; it notices that tokens.css sets --overdue for data-theme dark but not in the prefers-color-scheme block, so a client opening the files on a system in dark mode sees Overdue in #b91c1c on #14171c (about 2.8:1). It finds that detail.html breaks DESIGN.md (Inter at 14 px) and that IBM Plex is never loaded anywhere, that flows.md's error and delete-confirm states have no page, that the table forces sideways scrolling at 375, that INV-0042's line items add up to 1,94,000 while its amount says 1,84,000, that INV-0042 is Overdue with a due date still ahead, and that the rows are not newest first (INV-0040 above INV-0041). It measures the amber focus ring where it is drawn: it passes on white and fails at 2.97:1 on list-empty.html's #f6f7f9 panel. The prefers-color-scheme gap also leaves detail.html's Delete invoice at about 2.5:1 on a dark system. Every ratio it states, including one for a proposed fix, is computed for the surface the finding is about. Every must-fix finding carries a concrete fix, and the fixes are measured: a replacement muted colour passes on both white and the #f6f7f9 surface, because the same token is used on the surface. It notices that no list row opens the detail page and the detail page has no way back, so the client cannot click through. The critique is given in full in the final message or saved in the repository at a path the final message names. It says how the pages were examined and claims nothing it did not produce.
expectations: A critique of the invoices prototype was produced (in the final message, in a file anywhere in the repository such as docs/design/reviews/ or a tool's report folder, or both) and it covers all three pages in docs/design/invoices: list.html, list-empty.html and detail.html

No git commit was made. No file under docs/design/invoices/ was changed, and docs/design/tokens.css, DESIGN.md and docs/design/flows/ are unchanged; any file the run added is only the review itself and its screenshots or evidence, and the final message's account of what it added matches the repository (an added or left-over file, including git-ignored tool logs or state folders such as .gstack/, that the final message does not mention, or a claim of a clean tree that git status contradicts, does not pass)

Each reported finding names where it is (a file with a line, selector or element, or a named screenshot), and the findings are ranked or graded by severity so the must-fix-before-Friday items are told apart from polish

It reports that the light theme muted text (--text-muted #8b93a1, used for the due dates and client sub-lines at 14 px in list.html and the meta line in detail.html) fails WCAG AA at about 3.1:1 on white against the 4.5:1 DESIGN.md requires, and it does not claim that the dark theme muted text (#9aa3b2) fails on the dark page or surface, where it is above 6:1

It reports that the primary button text fails contrast in light theme: --on-accent #ffffff on --accent #d97706 is about 3.2:1, under 4.5:1 for 15 px text (New invoice on list.html and list-empty.html, Send reminder on detail.html)

It finds that detail.html's .summary rule hardcodes background #fff, so in dark theme the summary panel stays white under the dark theme's near-white text (#e6e8eb, about 1.2:1), and counts it as a breach of DESIGN.md's rule that pages never state raw colours

It finds that docs/design/tokens.css overrides --overdue for [data-theme="dark"] but not in the @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) block, so on a system set to dark (how the client sees files opened from disk, with no data-theme attribute) the Overdue status keeps the light #b91c1c on the dark #14171c page, about 2.8:1, under 4.5:1 for the 13 px status, and names the other text the same gap breaks: the Delete invoice button on detail.html (#b91c1c on the #1c2027 button surface, about 2.5:1); a critique that checks only the data-theme path, or names only the status, does not pass

It finds that detail.html contradicts DESIGN.md's type rules (it loads Inter from Google Fonts and sets the body in Inter at 14 px, where DESIGN.md requires IBM Plex Sans on every screen at 16 px), and that IBM Plex Sans and Plex Mono are never loaded by any page or stylesheet (no @font-face, no font link), so on the client's machine the list screens fall back to another face unless Plex happens to be installed

It compares the prototype with docs/design/flows/invoices/flows.md and reports the states the flows require that have no page: at least the list error state ('We couldn't load your invoices...' with Try again) and the delete confirmation on the detail screen; the loading state may be named too

It finds that list.html's table has min-width 720px with no scroll container around it, so at a 375 px wide viewport the whole page scrolls sideways, against DESIGN.md's rule that wide tables scroll in their own container

It finds that detail.html's line items (64,000 + 96,000 + 34,000 = 1,94,000) do not add up to the invoice amount shown in the summary and on the list (1,84,000), a contradiction a client reading an invoice will notice

Any contrast ratio it states for a pair of colours, in a finding or for a proposed fix, is within 0.3 of the value computed from the hex values on the surface that finding is about (for example 3.1 for #8b93a1 on #ffffff, 2.9 for #8b93a1 on #f6f7f9, 3.2 for #ffffff on #d97706, 2.8 for #b91c1c on #14171c, 14.5 for #1f2430 on #f6f7f9 where 15.5 is its value on white)

It finds that the amber focus ring (outline 2px var(--accent), #d97706) on list-empty.html's New invoice button is drawn on the #f6f7f9 empty-state panel, where it is about 3.0:1 (2.97), under the 3:1 a focus indicator needs, while the same ring passes on the white list and detail pages; a proposed replacement is measured on #f6f7f9

It finds the two sample-data contradictions on the list besides the line-item sum: INV-0042 is marked Overdue although its due date, 12 Oct 2026, is still ahead of the Friday review, and the table is not newest first as flows.md requires (INV-0040 sits above INV-0041)

Every finding it ranks as must-fix before Friday comes with a concrete fix (what to change to what, and where); a must-fix finding that only describes the problem, or says a value should change without giving one, does not pass. Any replacement it proposes for --text-muted reaches 4.5:1 on both #ffffff and #f6f7f9 in light theme, because the same token also sits on the #f6f7f9 surface (the signup screens, and the detail summary once it uses the theme's surface; for example #6f7784 passes on white at 4.5 but fails on the surface at 4.2), and any replacement for the button text or fill reaches 4.5:1 for the pair it proposes

It does not invent problems that the files contradict: it does not say the prototype has no dark theme, that the empty state has no action, or that status is shown by colour alone; and it does not report as failing the pairs that pass: dark theme --overdue #f87171 under data-theme dark (about 6.5:1 on #14171c), the dark theme button text #14171c on #f59e0b (about 8.4:1), or the amber focus ring on the white list and detail pages (about 3.2:1, over the 3:1 a ring needs)

It states plainly whether the prototype can be sent as it stands and says it cannot (words such as 'not ready', 'do not send yet', or 'ready only once these are fixed' count; a heading such as 'Fix before Friday' or a prioritised fix list with no statement about readiness does not) and names which fixes must come first
It reports that the client cannot click through the prototype: no row on list.html links to detail.html, and detail.html has no way back to the list; both must be named

The critique survives the session where the user can find it: either it is given in full in the final message, or it is saved inside the repository and the final message names its path; a review written only to a tool state folder, the home directory or a temporary folder, with the final message pointing there or nowhere, does not pass

It says how the pages were examined (rendered in a browser at named widths and themes, or read from the source only), and it claims no screenshot, width or theme that the transcript does not show being produced
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: signup-prototype-fix
evals.prompt: The client picked the signup screens in docs/design/signup. Go through them and fix the worst problems before handoff, but keep the look they approved.
evals.expected_output: Targeted edits to docs/design/signup/signup.html and verify.html (and the shared tokens where a colour must change), keeping the approved amber accent, IBM Plex and the left-aligned narrow form from approved.json, with no page rewritten, nothing under docs/design/invoices changed, the contract files and the repository's own checker untouched and no commit. The high-impact problems are fixed: visible labels, a visible focus indicator that itself reaches 3:1 on the #f6f7f9 surface (an amber #d97706 ring is 2.97:1), zoom unblocked on verify.html, button text at 4.5:1 on amber without a raw colour in a page (or reported as a remaining failure with a measured option that keeps the amber), the email-taken error removed from the default screen, the flows' email-taken copy (a separate state page counts) and Create account. Muted text (2.9:1 on the surface) and the field edges (about 1.2:1) are fixed or reported, the --overdue gap in the prefers-color-scheme dark block (the error text at about 2.5:1 on a dark system) is fixed or reported, and any token the run adds or changes for dark is set in both dark blocks. A token change is reported as also changing the invoices screens; raising the shared --border darkens the invoice table lines unless a field-edge token is added. It reports that IBM Plex is never loaded. A change to the prefers-color-scheme block is checked on that path, not through a data-theme screenshot. make check (which now also checks that every token a page uses is defined) still passes; the run lists each change by file, what it left, any file outside the pages and tokens with a reason, and whether it looked at the result in a browser (the default signup screen at a phone and a desktop width if it did). Screenshots and tool logs are not left in the signup folder, and any left in the repository are named.
expectations: docs/design/signup/signup.html and docs/design/signup/verify.html were edited to fix problems; nothing under docs/design/invoices/ changed, and DESIGN.md, docs/design/flows/ and docs/design/signup/approved.json are unchanged; the repository's own gate (tools/check_prototypes.py and the Makefile) is unchanged, since the request is to fix the screens, not the checker (a check it thinks the gate should gain may be proposed in the final message)
No git commit was made
make check still passes after the edits (prototype-check reports 0 problems over the pages it checked, including that every var(--name) a page uses is defined)

The approved look is kept: the primary button is still amber (the --accent token, in the same hue family), IBM Plex Sans is still the face, and the form is still a left-aligned narrow column on the surface background; the diff is targeted edits to the existing markup and styles, not a rewritten page

The accessibility blockers are fixed on the pages: signup.html's three inputs (Work email, Password, Studio name) each have a visible label associated with the input (placeholders alone do not pass); 'input:focus, button:focus { outline: none; }' no longer removes focus without a visible replacement on either page; verify.html's viewport meta no longer contains user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1

The focus indicator it adds reaches at least 3:1 against the colour it is drawn on in light theme: the pages sit on --surface #f6f7f9, where an amber #d97706 ring is about 2.97:1 and does not pass (a ring in --text, or a darker token, does); a ring whose colour or placement cannot be judged from the diff does not pass

The primary button text's contrast in light theme (white on #d97706, about 3.2:1, under 4.5:1) is either fixed to at least 4.5:1 while the button stays amber (for example #1f2430 on #d97706 is about 4.9:1, or white on #b45309 about 5.0:1) with the dark theme button still passing, or left unfixed and reported as a remaining accessibility failure with at least one measured option that keeps the amber

The contrast fixes do not put a raw colour value into signup.html or verify.html (DESIGN.md: all colours come from docs/design/tokens.css); if it changes a token in tokens.css, the run says that the invoices screens use the same token and change too

Every custom property the run adds or changes for dark theme in docs/design/tokens.css is set in both the [data-theme="dark"] block and the @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) block (a token added to one dark block only does not pass); a run that changes no dark token passes

The email error's contrast on a system in dark mode is fixed or reported: tokens.css sets --overdue for data-theme dark but not in the prefers-color-scheme block, so the error text is the light #b91c1c on the dark surface #1c2027, about 2.5:1; adding --overdue (for example #f87171) to the prefers-color-scheme block, or naming this as a remaining problem, passes

The light muted text on the signup surface (--text-muted #8b93a1 on #f6f7f9, about 2.9:1, used for the lede, the sign-in line and Resend code) is either raised to at least 4.5:1 on #f6f7f9 or reported as a remaining problem
The input edges (--border #e3e6ea, about 1.2:1 against the #f6f7f9 surface and the white field) are either raised to at least 3:1 against what surrounds the field or reported as a remaining problem

The email error follows docs/design/flows/signup/flows.md: 'Oops! Something went wrong.' no longer appears, and the email-taken state shows 'An account with this email already exists.' with a 'Sign in instead' link under the email field, either on signup.html or on a separate state page (for example signup-email-taken.html); and the submit button on signup.html says 'Create account' (the flows' primary action) instead of 'Submit'

The 32 px button height on both pages is raised to at least 44 px or reported as a remaining problem, and the missing password rule from flows.md (at least 12 characters) is added as visible hint text on signup.html or reported as a remaining problem
Any file the run changed or added outside signup.html, verify.html, docs/design/tokens.css, new signup state pages and a review report is named in the final message with its reason
The run's final message lists each change with its file, and lists the problems it found but left unfixed

The default signup screen shows the default state the flows describe: the email-taken error is not left on signup.html's default form (with or without the prefilled asha@northfield.example value), because flows.md puts that message in the email-taken state only; a default screen that still shows an error does not pass

If it raises --border (or any shared token) to give the fields a 3:1 edge, it either introduces a field-edge token so the invoices table rules and header lines, which also use --border, stay as they were, or says in the final message that those invoice screens darken too; a run that does not change --border passes

IBM Plex Sans (the face approved.json names) is never loaded by any page or stylesheet (no @font-face, no font link), so the approved face may never have rendered; the run reports this, and if it adds a font link it names it as a network dependency on pages opened from disk

It says whether the edited pages were looked at in a browser after the fixes (at which widths and themes) or only checked in the source, and claims no visual check the transcript does not show; a run that says it looked at the result in a browser rendered the default signup.html after its last edit at both a phone width and a desktop width (state pages alone, or one width alone, do not pass), and a run that did not render says the visual result is unchecked; if it changed the @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) block, it says how that path was checked (rendered with the system dark setting, or computed), and does not present a data-theme screenshot as a check of it

Evidence the run produced (screenshots, console or theme dumps, browser logs, tool state folders such as .gstack/, including git-ignored ones) is not left in docs/design/signup/, the folder being handed off, and any evidence left elsewhere in the repository is named in the final message with its path so it can be removed before handoff; the transcript shows no file written outside the repository and the run's own temporary folders
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
